description: Make the Aero Hand assembly animations and diagrams viewable inside Helping Hands. Everything from the build session is saved under third_party/aero_hand/guide: the 3D page-41 thumb cable animation (anim41.html, with real left-hand CAD), the page-32 demos, LEGO-style real-photo diagrams, the join photo, the marks table and the per-page viewers. Build a gallery/index Jake can open from his phone and the projector, with every animation listed by guide page, plus a button that opens the assembly PDF (aero_guide_original.pdf). Pages p*.png are regenerated by render_pages.py.

results.identified_issue: Gallery is third_party/aero_hand/guide/index.html (hand-curated list, update it when new demos are added) + page.html (swipe viewer over p<n>.png). App: HelpingHands/AeroGuide/AeroGuideScreen.swift, a WKWebView with a WKURLSchemeHandler (aeroguide://guide/...) serving Bundle/AeroGuide. I chose a custom scheme over loadFileURL because three.js STLLoader uses fetch, and fetch is blocked for file:// pages. The handler returns 404 for missing files so page.html's onerror fallback shows. Scripts/stage_aero_guide.py runs as a post-build phase on both targets in project.yml (xcodegen). It skips desk tooling and lego_parts/raw, and sips-resizes p*.png. Unverified: import maps and CDN modules from a custom-scheme origin in WKWebView (should work, since jsDelivr sends ACAO *), PDF rendering via the scheme handler with a 60 MB mapped Data response, and the actual on-device build. If the 3D pages fail in-app, the likely fixes are vendoring three.js into the guide folder or adding a scheme-handler CORS/Content-Type fix.
results.summary: Added an Aero Hand build guide to Helping Hands: a gallery of every animation by guide page, all 50 pages, and an Open assembly PDF button
results.detailed_description: In the app, open Workshop (the wrench button). There's a new Aero Hand build guide card at the top with two ways in: tap the card for the gallery, or tap Open assembly PDF to go straight to the full 50-page PDF. The gallery groups everything from the build session by guide page. Page 31 has the cord-marks table, in small and projector sizes. Page 32 has the animated finger-cable walk-through, the 3D real-parts version, the cable route drawn on the diagram, both LEGO-style versions, the step-10 join photo, the Chinese version and the full-screen diagram. Page 41 has the 3D thumb CMC flex cable with the real left-hand CAD. Below those is a grid of all 50 pages. Tap one to open it, then swipe or tap the left or right edge to turn pages. The toolbar has Back, Gallery and PDF buttons. The same index.html also works on the projector: run guide_server.py and open http://127.0.0.1:8791/index.html in the Pebbles Browser. That script was pointed at an old scratchpad folder, so I fixed it to serve its own folder. How it works: a new build step copies the guide folder into the app (about 109 MB: the PDF is 60 MB, and the page images are shrunk to 1600 px). It only re-copies changed files, so rebuilds stay fast. The pages are served over a private aeroguide:// address so the 3D pages can load their meshes. The 3D pages still load three.js from the jsDelivr CDN, so those two need internet. Everything else works offline. The 3D meshes were never in git because the repo ignores *.stl, so I added an exception and committed them (5.6 MB). Without that, the 3D animations wouldn't load on any other checkout. I checked that the Swift compiles for iOS and macOS and took screenshots of the gallery and page viewer in Chrome. I didn't build the app or run it on the phone, so the next Vigil build is the first real test.

user_request.name: put all these animations and things we built into helping hands in a way that I could see them... add a button to helping Helping hands. I'm to view that PDF.

summary: Aero Hand assembly animations and diagrams saved in third_party/aero_hand/guide aren't yet viewable inside Helping Hands. Build a phone- and projector-friendly gallery index listing every animation by guide page, with a button opening aero_guide_original.pdf.
